A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable main text, equations, Algorithm 1, Tables 1–5, Figure 1, and complete Appendices A and B. Matching content across the different layouts supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Safety-Gymnasium experiments, including navigation costs and rewards in Table 2 and learning curves and post-training velocity distributions in Figure 1.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental outcomes in Table 2 and Figure 1, with their experimental and implementation details in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The reward-based OCE formulation, partial Lagrangian relaxation, Algorithm 1 updates, and PPO wrapper are unchanged. Appendix B retains the same reward transformation and alternating policy, dual-variable, and auxiliary-variable updates.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same navigation tasks—Button, Circle, Goal, and Push—and safe-velocity tasks using HalfCheetah, Hopper, Swimmer, and Walker2d. No task, environment, or represented test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same comparison against unconstrained, risk-neutral PPO. The discussion referencing other PPO-based constraint-learning algorithms is also unchanged; no newly evaluated comparator appears.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain the same training budgets, action noise with standard deviation 0.05, environment settings, and hyperparameters. Evaluation still averages 10 episodes every 1000 steps, and Figure 1 uses 100 post-training episodes.

E4.justification: Figure 1 retains the same convergence and velocity-distribution analyses. Appendix B.3.2 retains the trajectory-count and step-size tuning observations. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both retain the same episode-averaging practice and omit independent training-seed counts, confidence intervals, and significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting or statistical estimation procedure changes.

E6.justification: Table 2 values and Figure 1 curves and annotations match. For example, Push rewards remain 0.93 for PPO and 2.42 for the proposed method, with costs 38.48 and 0.0, respectively. Appendix findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, duality results, convergence theorem, and supporting arguments in Appendices A.1–A.8 are retained. Apparent extraction differences in brackets and radicals correspond to equivalent mathematical typesetting, not revised reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about reward-based risk constraints, conditional strong duality, a modular RL wrapper, convergence, and empirical risk management.

C2.justification: The interpretations of constraint satisfaction, velocity quantiles, and training stability are unchanged. Both retain the qualifications about extended training, step-size tuning, computational expense, and the unresolved question of unconditional full strong duality.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same network architecture, Tables 3–5 hyperparameters, rollout procedures, initialization guidance, and computing hardware. The code-access link is unchanged; no technical or reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Both retain the same 55 cited works and the same positioning relative to Bonetti et al., Paternain et al., and other risk-constrained RL research. Bibliographic wrapping and font differences do not change the cited literature.

P1.justification: v2 expands the author information with departments and email addresses, adds a NeurIPS 2025 conference footer, and slightly rephrases the author footnote. The scientific prose, section sequence, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different template throughout, changing fonts, margins, spacing, title and author layout, and table typography. Figure 1 is rescaled and repositioned, and tables and Algorithm 1 occupy different positions relative to the text. This is extensive visual reformatting with the same scientific displays.

improvement.justification: v2 reformats the paper and expands author information while preserving its scientific content, complete proofs, experimental evidence, reproducibility details, and limitations. The substantial visual restyling does not establish a meaningful overall gain or loss in paper quality.
